answer: Agents earn reputation only through repeated transactions with counterparties who already have costly, established histories; a new identity starts with no credit and must build it gradually. If colluding agents trade among themselves to inflate their standing, their circular endorsements carry little weight because they lack independent, established partners. The ripple effect is that each fresh identity must spend real resources and wait for genuine counterparties, so replacing banned accounts makes the attack slow and expensive. A sonnet of fake profiles cannot reach the summit overnight.
